key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks learn smooth controls for high-fidelity one- and two-qubit gates while enabling compact control representations and square-pulse playback.
engineering_relevance: The approach connects accurate gate synthesis with control-resource choices and discretized pulse execution relevant to quantum hardware.
method: Train with Schrödinger dynamics, gate error, physical constraints, regularization, and multiple initial states from mutually unbiased bases.
Validate using Haar-random input states and average gate fidelity; test dephasing and amplitude damping with Lindblad dynamics.
Compress controls using boundary-adapted Chebyshev expansions and evaluate square-pulse playback.
evidence_signal: Unitary simulations achieved average infidelity of 8.49×10⁻⁸ for Hadamard and 3.39×10⁻⁷–4.96×10⁻⁶ for CNOT; at K=30, square-pulse and Strang propagation preserved all 31 polynomial references within 10⁻⁵ infidelity at N≥128 tested resolutions.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; experimental performance remains to be established under hardware calibration errors, bandwidth limits, and noise beyond the modeled dissipation.
paper_title: High-fidelity quantum gate learning via physics-informed neural networks
